subject: english-language
title: Models of Spread
welcome_lead: How exactly does a change ripple through a speech community? Map the wave, the s-curve and the lexical diffusion.
meta_desc: Wave model, lexical diffusion, S-curve and random fluctuation models of language change at A-Level.
final_note: You have surveyed the engines of spread — wave, s-curve, diffusion and chance — that move change through a community.

concepts.def: Johannes Schmidt's 1872 model — change radiates outward from an innovation centre, weakening with distance.
Chen's S-curve plots adoption against time: slow start, rapid uptake, plateau.
William Wang's theory — phonological change spreads word by word through the lexicon, not all at once.
Charles Hockett's view — small accidental variations accumulate into systematic change without overall purpose.
Change attributed to influence of a previous or contact language (Celtic on English, Norman on Middle English).
Halliday — change happens because speakers need to express new meanings.

walkthroughs.body_html: Schmidt's wave model imagines change radiating from London-like centres into surrounding regions. Innovations weaken with distance and time, producing dialect zones.

Wang showed that sound change does not affect all words simultaneously. Some words shift early, others lag.

The TRAP-BATH split in southern England has affected bath and laugh but not maths — diffusion in action.

Hockett's random fluctuation theory frames change as the accumulation of tiny accidental variants, like genetic drift.

The view emphasises stochastic processes rather than functional purpose.

mcqs.q: Is language change a sign of decline?
options: Language change shows that standards are falling and English is being ruined.
No — modern linguistics treats change as natural and continuous, not as decay. Every language has always been changing and will continue to.
It is the stage where children memorise long stories.
Language change only happens in informal speech, not in writing.

mcqs.q: What is the telegraphic stage of child language development?
options: Chomsky said children should be taught grammar from age two.
Around age 2-3, children produce short utterances containing content words but omitting function words and inflections (e.g. 'mummy gone shop').
It is the stage when children first start using a telephone.
It is the stage where children memorise long stories.

mcqs.q: What did Chomsky propose about language acquisition?
options: It is the stage where children memorise long stories.
Chomsky said children learn language entirely by copying adults.
Children possess an innate Language Acquisition Device — an inborn capacity for grammar — because exposure alone cannot account for how rapidly and uniformly children learn complex syntax.
Chomsky said children should be taught grammar from age two.
